title: Resolve entitlement mismatch during API key stitching for subaccount-linked requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers reported sudden quota surges and incorrect org-level billing when they performed API key stitching (linking a new integration key to an existing subaccount). Symptoms: tokens created during key-stitching flows were being attributed to the parent org rather than the intended subaccount/project, causing both overdrawn project quotas and inflated org-level usage. Scope: reproduces across Hosted API and Dedicated; occurs when an integration token is issued while a pending key-rebind state exists (key aliasing + delayed cache invalidation). This ticket tracks diagnosis, temporary mitigations, and a permanent fix path that preserves existing guarantees (no retroactive billing changes without manual approval).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create parent org with two subaccounts (proj-A, proj-B) and enable integration tokens
2) Issue integration token T1 scoped to proj-A; record attribution_id = A
3) Initiate key-stitching: issue new token T2 and rebind alias so both tokens coexist temporarily
4) Trigger high-throughput calls using T2 while backend key-resolution still references old alias mappings
5) Observe that usage events are recorded with attribution_id = parent-org (null project) in billing DB and Quota service
6) Confirm logs show race between alias-rewrite propagation and attribution-cache eviction (key-store -> attribution service -> billing pipeline).
analysis: Root cause hypothesis: race between token alias rewrite and attribution cache leading to fallback attribution path that resolves to org-level when project mapping not found.
Attribution service currently falls back to the token owner record in the legacy token table when project lookup fails; this legacy path uses org-owner ID and doesn’t respect recent alias bindings.
Eviction window: 30s TTL on in-memory attribution cache; alias write is async and writes to token-store with eventual consistency across replicas.

Additional failure mode: metrics ingestion pipeline deduplicates tokens based on raw key fingerprint; when a stitched token fingerprint changes, downstream join to project metadata fails and billing pipeline assigns a null project tag which is interpreted as org-level billing.
proposed_fix: Immediate mitigation (hotfix): extend attribution cache TTL to 5 minutes and temporarily disable fallback-to-legacy-owner in attribution service for keys in 'stitching' state. Deploy to hosted and dedicated regions in a controlled rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Short-term rollback-safe change: make alias-write path synchronous w.r.t. attribution metadata update (write-through) so that token-store update and attribution cache update are ordered in a transaction boundary for stitched tokens.

Long-term solution: redesign attribution resolution to consult authoritative project mapping table first, then fall back to token-owner only after a deterministic reconciliation window. Add explicit 'stitching' token state to token-store to avoid ambiguous lookups.
Add end-to-end unit & integration tests that simulate concurrent alias rewrites and high-throughput meters to prevent regressions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Deploy hotfix to staging and run synthetic billing regression tests (24h) against workload generator.
Phase 1: Canary to 10% of traffic in us-west-2 for Hosted API and one Dedicated customer (non-production) — monitor quiescent error rate and billing attribution metrics for 6 hours.
Phase 2: Ramp to 50% after 6h if no regressions; monitor for 48h.
Phase 3: Full deployment and schedule follow-up jobs to retroactively reconcile last 2 hours of misattributed events for affected customers (requires finance approval).
Rollback: if org-level attribution increases more than baseline by >2x for any canary host, rollback immediately and open incident bridge.
acceptance_criteria: All synthetic reproduction cases no longer emit org-level attribution when token-stitching occurs.
Observed reduction of misattributed billing events to < 0.01% across canary traffic within 24h of deployment.
Integration tests added and passing in CI covering alias rewrite + concurrent request patterns.
Finance and Customer Success sign-off on reconciliation plan for impacted customers.
